pillars.name: MemChorus Recall Verification
pillars.description: Verifies actual recall injection in turns, NOT doctor-probe status.
pillars.critical_constraint: Per #312: on_grok profile, pinned doctor passed while recall injection was off. Gateway Python cannot import memchorus, and on_pre_llm_call returns nothing with no warning.
pillars.check_method: Verify MemChorus contribution block exists in turn's system prompt (content markers in request dumps; doctor probe as contrast signal only, parsed from stdout not exit code)
pillars.evidence_source: request_dump_*.json under <profile>/sessions/ (API-failure captured turns — the only on-disk copy of a turn's real prompt)
pillars.wrapper_marker: [MemChorus Memory Recall] (block present, may contain no content — NOT a landing)

verdicts.green: content marker in >=1 of the last N captured turns, landing within --max-landing-age-hours (default 72h)
verdicts.yellow: #312 signature (probe green, no content landing) OR stale evidence (landing older than freshness window)
verdicts.red: no content in last N captured turns and probe red/unknown; or zero captured turns with probe red

pillars.false_positive_threshold: Doctor-green but no actual recall landing in 3+ consecutive turns
pillars.false_negative_threshold: No doctor probe result but recall actually lands

documented_misses.case: green on 461h-old landing (2026-11-03) with zero captured turns since
documented_misses.fix: freshness window (--max-landing-age-hours, default 72h) downgrades to yellow

documented_misses.case: red verdict while 2026-11-22 session actively receives injected recall block (dumps only capture API-failure turns; probe reflects gateway interpreter, not session interpreter)
documented_misses.fix_next: active in-process probe of on_pre_llm_call under the profile's actual Python asserting non-empty context_items

pillars.name: Polygraph CLI Health
pillars.description: Ensures the Polygraph CLI is usable and no P0/P1 blockers exist.
pillars.check_method: Two probes combined: (1) run `python3 scripts/run_polygraph.py --help` in the Polygraph repo and capture the real exit code (non-zero -> red); (2) list OPEN issues on the GitHub repo and classify each P0 (CLI cannot start/parse - import/startup failure, entrypoint crash), P1 (CLI runs but result wrong/unusable-in-context - hardcoded model, OPSEC/hardcoded home paths), P2 (non-blocking). critical_issues = P0 + P1 count. P0 import failures are cross-referenced against the live --help probe to detect stale issues (reproduces: false).
pillars.blocked_pr_threshold: Any P0 or P1 polygraph issue blocking tool usage

verdicts.green: CLI --help exit 0 AND no open P0/P1 issues
verdicts.yellow: CLI --help exit 0 BUT >=1 open P0/P1 issue (tooling partially blocked)
verdicts.red: CLI --help exit != 0 (CLI not usable at all)

pillars.false_positive_threshold: CLI --help exit 0 (green) but a real run against the model endpoint still fails -- --help only proves importability + arg-parsing, not a verified result
pillars.false_negative_threshold: An open P0 CLI-import issue flagged blocking, but the current code no longer triggers that failure (stale issue over-penalises a working tool)

documented_misses.case: CLI --help exit 0 (would be green for the usability probe) but a real run `--tests 1A --base-url http://127.0.0.1:9 --no-tools` fails: '1A ERROR - All connection attempts failed', Overall Grade FAIL, exit 1. --help proves importability + arg-parsing only, not that the tool produces a verified result.

issue #12 (P0, startup import failure on a missing local package) is OPEN so the blocker scan flags yellow, but the current code no longer imports that package and --help returns exit 0 from every context (repo root, neutral cwd, <profile-a> skill dir) - the failure no longer reprodues.
documented_misses.fix_next: check records reproduces:false on P0 import issues whose described failure the live --help probe does not show, so the stale issue is visible in evidence rather than silently over-penalising

pillars.name: Task Completion Rate
pillars.description: % of tasks completing without blocking or rework.
pillars.check_method: Read the shared kanban SQLite store (~/.hermes/kanban.db, same rows the kanban_list/kanban_show tools read) READ-ONLY. Window = last N (default 20) tasks with status='done'. A task is CLEAN iff (a) it has zero `blocked` events in task_events (covers every block kind: dependency/needs_input/capability/transient — the board's record of a blocked or needs_input status change) AND (b) every row in task_runs has a successful outcome (`completed`, `review_requested`); any of `blocked`, `crashed`, `timed_out`, `spawn_failed`, `gave_up`, `reclaimed`, `changes_requested` counts as rework. completion_rate = clean / total.
pillars.evidence_source: kanban SQLite store: tasks + task_events + task_runs (never the board UI)
pillars.critical_constraint: Read-only: check never modifies task data; auto-correction for low-rate trends = comment or new card, not a silent edit

verdicts.green: completion rate > 80% over last N tasks
verdicts.yellow: 60-80% completion rate, OR fewer than 10 tasks in window (insufficient data)

pillars.false_positive_threshold: Clean run history (one `completed` run, zero blocked events) on a task whose DELIVERED WORK later required follow-up fix tasks on the same issue — completion gate passed, work still failed downstream
pillars.false_negative_threshold: Task penalised as rework/blocked (crashed runs or a blocked event) but the work ultimately succeeded — a delayed success, counted as a failure by design

documented_misses.case: t_caa89f9b ("wing_isolation: accept {PROFILE}_{CATEGORY} as NATIVE for owning profile") shows ONE `completed` run and zero blocked events — clean by this measure — yet issue #304 still required two later [FIX] tasks (t_f360c2e8, t_468a6223, "Fix wing_isolation flags owning-profile wings as foreign") because the delivered code was wrong. Same pattern: t_448d9258 (qa+merge #306, clean) followed by t_b794de90 ("#308 follow-up: platform guards for 2 Windows test artifacts").

t_c4232521 ("memchorus-recall retrieve: flat-file fallback") ran 3x crashed (2x "owner admission settled failed", 1x worker exited without a lifecycle call) before one successful `completed` run — this check counts it as rework, but the deliverable landed and the work succeeded; the verdict is a delayed-success penalty, not a failed task. t_fd00e142 (blocked on a behavioral guard, then completed) is the same class.
documented_misses.fix_next: distinguish transient-infrastructure rework (crashed/reclaimed) from work-content rework (blocked/changes_requested) in metrics so a green rate is not silently eroded by spawn flakiness

pillars.name: Cross-Agent Communication Health
pillars.description: DM delivery success rate between agents.
pillars.check_method: Parse hermes-dm-* scratch logs for failed deliveries

phase_gate_rules.requirement: No Phase N+1 until documented miss in Phase N
phase_gate_rules.miss_definition: Case where check said healthy (green) but work failed, OR check said unhealthy (yellow/red) but work succeeded
phase_gate_rules.resolution: Miss becomes next change to the check, not a note in chat
